title: Permutation in String
description:
Given two strings `s1` and `s2`, return `true` if `s2` contains a permutation of `s1`, or `false` otherwise.

In other words, return `true` if one of `s1`'s permutations is a contiguous substring of `s2`.
constraints: s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: Two strings are permutations of each other if and only if they have the exact same character frequencies.
Since any valid permutation in s2 must have length s1.length, slide a fixed-size window of length s1.length across s2.
Maintain a 26-element frequency count for s1 and the current window, along with a counter of how many of the 26 letters currently match, to update each step in O(1) time.

examples.explanation: s2 contains one permutation of s1 ("ba") starting at index 3.
No contiguous substring of length 2 in s2 contains both 'a' and 'b', so return false.
s2 contains "cda" starting at index 1, which is a permutation of "adc".
